source: Kandal Provincial Department of Agriculture (មន្ទីរកសិកម្មខេត្តកណ្តាល), "ដំណំពោត" (Corn Crop / Zea mays production manual), 2015
text:
Corn is a plant with the scientific name Zea mays, belonging to the grass family Poaceae. It originated in Central America (Mexico and Guatemala), where people first began domesticating it about 7,000 years ago.

Root system: corn has a fibrous root system (no taproot). The main roots grow from the base of the seed's radicle, forming the primary root system, and additional roots also emerge from nodes above ground, called brace/prop roots. Roots can extend down to about 2 meters deep. The root system spreads about 0.5 m to 2 m wide, with root hairs that can penetrate soil to a depth of about 20-30 cm (roughly 80% of root mass), and the root system can spread as far out as 1 meter from the stem base.

Stem: the corn stem is solid, thick, and fleshy inside. Stem height generally ranges from about 50 to 300 cm, varying by variety, climate/weather conditions, and the plant's growing environment. A single corn stem can have from about 8 to 38 nodes depending on variety, cultivation technique, and growing conditions -- typically a corn stem has about 21 nodes. On the surface, the stem has nodes arranged around it, with internodes between them. Each node has one leaf attached.

Leaf: the corn leaf is long, broad, and pointed at the tip, with a central midrib running the length of the blade; leaves alternate from one side of the stem to the other going up. The leaf is divided into three parts: the leaf sheath (which wraps around the stem), the leaf blade (ligule area), and the leaf edge/margin. A single corn plant typically bears 12 to 18 leaves. The leaf blade is generally about 10 to 15 cm wide and about 100 cm long.

Tassel (male flower, ផ្កាឈៀល / ផ្កាឈៀលពោត): the tassel is the male flower structure located at the top of the corn plant. Silk (ផ្កាព្រី / ear silk): the silk is the female flower/inflorescence, located within the leaf axil along the stem, and typically several silks appear in one plant, one of which usually develops into the primary, well-formed ear, referred to popularly as "sakor poat" (the corn ear).

Ear (ផ្លែ): botanically, what is called the corn ear (ផ្លែពោត) is the cluster of kernels bound together and wrapped in several layers of husk. An ear can be about 8 to 42 cm long, with a diameter that varies from about 3 to 5 cm. Each ear can bear from about 300 to 1,000 kernels.
